summary.text: Grace Lee is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for the open State Senate District 27 seat. She is the Assemblymember for District 65 in Lower Manhattan, first elected in 2022, and previously co-founded a parent-led environmental coalition and a beauty products company. According to the Assembly, she is the first Korean American woman elected to the New York State Legislature and chairs the Assembly Asian Pacific American Task Force; she is not seeking re-election to her Assembly seat.

paragraphs.text: Grace Lee is the daughter of immigrants, according to her Assembly biography; she has lived in Lower Manhattan for about 15 years per her 2020 Ballotpedia survey, and lives there with her husband and three young daughters.
She earned a B.A. in economics and philosophy from Columbia University in 2002 and an M.B.A. in finance and entrepreneurship from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business in 2010.
In 2018, according to her 2020 survey, she was the New York events director for Swing Left, a group focused on flipping the U.S. House.

Before running for office, Lee co-founded Children First, a parent-led coalition focused on mercury brownfield cleanup near the South Street Seaport, and co-founded Nine Naturals, a beauty products company.
She ran for Assembly District 65 in 2020 and lost the Democratic primary to incumbent Yuh-Line Niou.

In June 2022 she won the Democratic primary for the open Assembly District 65 seat, which includes the Financial District, Chinatown and the Lower East Side, and she won the November general election over Republican Helen Qiu, taking office in January 2023; she was re-elected in 2024 with 99.1% of the vote.

In the Assembly, Lee serves on the Banks, Children and Families, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Environmental Conservation, and Insurance committees and chairs the Asian Pacific American Task Force.
According to her Assembly biography, she sponsored the Hate Crimes Modernization Act and led legislation making New York the first state to recognize Lunar New Year as a statewide school holiday.
On June 23, 2026, she defeated former Assemblymember Yuh-Line Niou in the Democratic primary for Senate District 27, 62.5% to 37.3%.
